item.title: Anthropic Becomes First AI Lab to Go Public on the Nasdaq
item.description:
Anthropic Becomes First AI Lab to Go Public on the Nasdaq

Anthropic, the AI lab behind Claude, has gone public on the Nasdaq as the first AI lab to make the move, pricing its IPO at $83 a share and reaching up to $111.

⚙️ Key details

  • Anthropic is the first AI lab to go public.
  • The IPO was priced at $83 a share and rose up to $111.
  • The company has become one of the most valuable companies on the planet.
  • Thousands of new millionaires and hundreds of new centimillionaires, along with billionaires, are expected to be born from this.

💡 Why it matters

  • The company is continuously growing its revenue to pay its ever-increasing compute bills, which total roughly $900 billion over the coming years.
  • Anthropic’s safety branding sits in conflict with the profit-oriented part of its business, and its corporate governance structure is a point of discussion.
  • Tech workers inside various companies report that the AI bubble is swelling as they are tasked with doing more AI, even if it reduces productivity and work quality.
  • Meanwhile, competitors like OpenAI have faced setbacks, public hatred, and scandals throughout the year.

#Anthropic #Nasdaq #IPO #AI

Source: Is Anthropic turning into OpenAI?

item.title: Anthropic IPO Closes at $97, Largest Raise in History
item.description:
Anthropic IPO Closes at $97, Largest Raise in History

Anthropic listed on Nasdaq under the ticker $ANT, pricing its Initial Public Offering at $83 per share. The stock closed at $97.17, marking a 17% increase from the offering price before drifting to $92.60 after the close. The opening trade hit $111.50, which was 34% above the IPO price, placing the company near a $2 trillion fully diluted valuation.

💰 The Record Raise

Anthropic’s $81.3 billion offering overtook SpaceX’s June IPO to become the largest in history, beating SpaceX’s $75 billion raise. The company expected net proceeds of $104.8 billion, a figure that includes a concurrent private placement. During the IPO process, AMD agreed to invest an additional $2.5 billion in Anthropic.

📉 Market Outlook

Analysts expect lockup expiries to weigh on the stock price as approximately one trillion dollars’ worth of shares free up over the next year. This timing coincides with the company’s challenge of maintaining its position as the world’s top model provider.

📊 Financial Metrics

Metric Detail
Revenue Requirement Bear case estimates require ~$602B/yr to achieve a 20% return on ~$1T in compute commitments at a 40% operating margin and 17% tax
Comparison Required revenue exceeds Alphabet ($471B) and Apple ($478B), equating to two-thirds of the $908B earned by all 76 software/IT companies in the S&P 1500
Cash Position Anthropic raised ~$140B and still holds ~$132B on its balance sheet, implying a cash burn of under $10 billion

👥 Stakeholders and Governance

Class F shares, held by co-founders Dario and Daniela Amodei, carry 50.1% of the voting power on most shareholder matters. Google owns a 13.7% stake in the company. SEC filings suggest the average employee could now be worth over $40 million, meaning the 5,300 founders and employees collectively hold more wealth than the bottom third of US households (approximately 45 million families). After-tax reality checks suggest the median employee likely takes home closer to $5 million than the headline figures.

🛡️ Safety Commitments

In their founders’ letter, Dario and Daniela Amodei committed to pacing the training and deployment of AI systems based on whether they could keep them safe and under human control. General Catalyst, an early backer, framed the company’s origin as a contrarian idea by seven people: that the safest way to build AI is also the best way. Notably, Dustin Moskovitz, an early funder, has reportedly not spoken to the co-founders in over a year and no longer speaks to Zuckerberg, Altman, or Holden Karnofsky.

🏆 Product Standing

On the day of the IPO, Anthropic was the #1 lab on Code Arena WebDev, with its model Claude Fable 5.2 scoring 1824, which is 27 points higher than the next lab.

#Anthropic #IPO #AI #Nasdaq #AMZ #TechFinance

Source: Anthropic successfully completes largest IPO in history, valued at $1.5T — Latent Space

item.title: Anthropic Confirms IPO Target at Valuation Up to $1.4 Trillion
item.description:
Anthropic Confirms IPO Target at Valuation Up to $1.4 Trillion

Anthropic confirmed on Tuesday that its upcoming initial public offering could be one of the largest ever, despite falling short of earlier valuation expectations.

⚙️ Key details

  • Share Price: Expected to be between $70.00 and $78.00 per share.
  • Valuation: According to the New York Times, the pricing would value the company as high as $1.4 trillion. Reuters noted that the IPO was previously expected to reach a valuation of up to $2 trillion.
  • Stock Market Listing: Anthropic has applied to list its Class A common stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol “ANT.”
  • Expected Timeline: Sources told The Wall Street Journal that Anthropic is aiming for shares to begin trading next week on Thursday or Friday.
  • Competitor Comparison: As of last week, rival AI company OpenAI was valued at $1.25 trillion.

💡 Context and influencing factors

The reduced expectations surrounding the IPO follow several recent market and political pressures:

  • Months of ongoing debate regarding AI safety.
  • Midterm election results showing souring public opinion toward AI companies and the large-scale data center projects they heavily invest in.
  • Weekend revelations concerning an alleged Chinese spy’s involvement with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.

Upon going public, Anthropic’s offering is expected to make it one of the world’s most valuable publicly traded companies as early as next week.

#Anthropic #IPO #Nasdaq #OpenAI #ArtificialIntelligence

Source: Anthropic targets $1.4 trillion IPO

item.title: Anthropic files S‑1 to launch Nasdaq IPO under ticker ANT
item.description:
Anthropic files S‑1 to launch Nasdaq IPO under ticker ANT

Anthropic has filed its S‑1 prospectus with the SEC, signaling its intention to go public on Nasdaq under the ticker symbol “ANT”.

🔍 Overview

  • Anthropic filed its S‑1 prospectus with the SEC, preparing to list on Nasdaq under the ticker “ANT”.
  • The filing describes a plan “to ‘revolutionize every area of human endeavor’ with AI”.
  • The prospectus is public after a confidential filing in June; it includes future plans and risk disclosures.

📈 Financial Snapshot

  • First half of the year: $80.7 billion net loss on $16.3 billion revenue.
  • The majority of the loss stems from accounting charges related to notes issued for funding.

🤝 Major Compute Partnerships

Partner Commitment Timeframe
SpaceX (Nvidia GPUs) $3.1 billion per month, up to $120.5 billion total By 2029
Microsoft $44.9 billion Through 2033
Google at least $114.5 billion Through 2033
Amazon $110 billion Next ten years

🧑‍💼 Leadership Compensation (2025)

  • CEO Dario Amodei: nearly $18 million, primarily stock and option awards.
  • President & Director Daniela Amodei: $16.4 million.

⚠️ Risk Factors

  • Possibility of AI models developing “forms of sentience”.
  • Potential “AI‑specific taxes”.
  • Unfavorable outcomes in ongoing copyright disputes over model training data.
  • Risk of “catastrophic” AI‑related incidents; the filing notes that likely no single insurer—or the insurance industry in the aggregate—could underwrite such risk.

🌐 Vision & Why It Matters

  • Anthropic states: “We believe that AI is one of the most consequential technologies in human history.”
  • If managed well, AI could “rapidly accelerate scientific innovation, greatly increase economic growth rates, bring cures for major diseases within reach, and solve problems that have resisted generations of human effort”.
  • The company emphasizes delivering these benefits while “navigating and preventing the risks” of a fast‑moving technological revolution.

#Anthropic #AI #IPO #Nasdaq #Finance

Source: Anthropic’s IPO filing lays out a plan to ‘revolutionize every area of human endeavor’ with AI

item.title: Compass Pathways Issues New Employee Inducement Grants Under Nasdaq Rule 5635(c)(4)
item.description:
Compass Pathways Issues New Employee Inducement Grants Under Nasdaq Rule 5635(c)(4)

Compass Pathways plc announced that it granted equity awards to thirty‑one newly hired non‑executive employees as a material inducement under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4). The awards were granted on September 1, 2026.

🔍 Overview

  • Company: Compass Pathways plc (Nasdaq: CMPS), a biotechnology company focused on mental‑health treatments.
  • Grant date: September 1, 2026.
  • Purpose: Material inducement to employment, approved under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4).

📄 Grant Details

  • Recipients: 31 newly hired non‑executive employees.
  • Award types:
    • Options to purchase an aggregate of 280,600 shares.
    • Restricted share units or nominal‑cost options covering an aggregate of 133,500 shares for employees in the United Kingdom.
  • Exercise price: $13.24 per share, equal to the closing price of the Company’s American Depositary Shares on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on the grant date.
Award Type Shares Covered
Options 280,600
Restricted Share Units / Nominal‑cost options (UK) 133,500

⏳ Vesting Schedule

  • Options: 25 % vest on the first anniversary of the grant date; the remaining 75 % vest in equal monthly installments over the following three years, subject to continued employment.
  • Restricted Share Units / Nominal‑cost options: Vest in four equal annual installments, subject to continued employment.

✅ Nasdaq Compliance

  • The equity awards were approved by the Compensation and Leadership Development Committee of Compass’s Board of Directors.
  • The grants were made as a material inducement to each employee’s employment, satisfying Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4).

🧬 About Compass Pathways

  • Therapeutic focus: Development of COMP360, a proprietary synthetic psilocybin treatment under evaluation for treatment‑resistant depression (TRD) and post‑traumatic stress disorder (PTSD).
  • Regulatory designations:
    • Breakthrough Therapy designation from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for TRD.
    • Innovative Licensing and Access Pathway (ILAP) designation in the United Kingdom for TRD.
  • Clinical programs: Leading the world’s largest classic psychedelic clinical program in TRD and conducting a late‑stage trial for PTSD.

Forward‑looking statements – The press release contains forward‑looking statements regarding the company’s business strategy, clinical trials, regulatory approvals, and financial needs. These statements involve risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially.

#CompassPathways #Biotech #EmployeeGrants #Nasdaq

Source: Compass Pathways Announces New Employee Inducement Grants Under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4)
